$comment: The releases of portal-netgl, and the state of the repo before it, as the Pages site snapshots them under /v/<version>/. `ref` is the last commit on main at that version (what the version shipped as), `demos` the apps that existed then, `docs` whether the responses site existed. scripts/write-versions.mjs folds this into /v/versions.json, .github/workflows/snapshot.yml rebuilds a version from its ref, and docs/rfcs/responses/img/generate.mjs draws the timeline from it. `layout: 'demo-root'` marks a snapshot whose Local portal demo is at its root (every version up to 0.6.8); from then on the site root is the summary page and the demo is at three/.

versions.label: Frame-RPC portals, before NetGL
versions.summary: Doors between three.js worlds: a halfspace stencil and an oblique clip; endpoints over local, iframe, Worker and headless transports shipping colour and packed-depth bitmaps; traversal; recursive portals; a server-side snapshot proxy.

versions.label: The command stream
versions.summary: A Proxy records a guest's WebGL2 calls, a shadow context answers them synchronously, the host replays them in its own context with handles interned and a frame-end marker; postMessage carries it. celestiary goes through a door unmodified but for a renderer hook: door-fit viewport remap, batches concatenated, autoClear rules. Published to npm on 2026-05-28.

versions.label: Checkpoint, screen policy, Cesium
versions.summary: A framework-agnostic guest core; the state checkpoint at each frame boundary; the screen policy (stencil, clears, blend) and screenFramebuffer; the same-page immediate link; Cesium as a guest through getWebGLStub, through a door and in place of a three.js Earth. The f → f′ shim model, the portal-layers 0.1 design and the lessons from celestiary's Cesium layers, which run in production.

versions.label: Tracked state
versions.summary: The checkpoint is built from tracked scalar state: no synchronous GL queries per guest frame (79 before).

versions.label: Inside the host's pass
versions.summary: clear: 'none' and sub-frames: a guest drawn several times in one host frame, inside the host's pass, against its depth (Cesium drawing Slop New York per frustum).

versions.label: Overlay, the view, cross-origin
versions.summary: The deck.gl / luma.gl host adapter (restore, where three invalidates), the overlay kind in the host's clip space, layer:view and the first control messages, postMessage transports pinned by origin on both ends, a three.js overlay guest. RFC 0001 starts the series.

versions.label: Wire 2
versions.summary: One batch per guest frame over a MessagePort, negotiated in the handshake; uploads sliced to the bytes a call reads; recorder-owned buffers transferred. A cross-site frame: 187 messages and 505 KB → 1 and 48 KB.

versions.label: Redraw folding
versions.summary: A redraw request restarts the fold window, so a guest frame that lands after a host draw still gets its own.

versions.label: No-draw shadow
versions.summary: shadowDraws: false skips the shadow context's draws for a guest that never reads back; the stream is unchanged.

versions.label: Host reprojection
versions.summary: A late overlay frame is corrected to the host's current view (gl_Position × VP_now · VP_frame⁻¹, the vertex shaders rewritten once); viewId on the frame-end says which view a frame was for.

versions.label: Opt-in shaders
versions.summary: A vertex shader that declares netgl_reproject applies the correction itself (wide lines keep their width).

versions.label: Viewport map
versions.summary: A frame drawn for one buffer size is mapped when the host's buffer changed size.

versions.label: Cesium shim passthrough
versions.summary: makeNetGLCesiumGuest passes shadowDraws through (0.6.5 had gone to the viewport map).

versions.label: Pixel sizes
versions.summary: A lagging frame's point sizes and line widths follow the host's pixel ratio.

versions.label: Parts
versions.summary: Several draws for one view, each to its own target: part on the frame-end and beforeFrame on the receiver (celestiary's night lights from a guest page). The RFC responses and this site.

versions.label: Deferred deletes
versions.summary: Any frame can be re-run: deletes wait for the next new frame, their implicit unbinds happen in place (RFC 0003's first step, for celestiary's late Cesium frames).

versions.label: Named screen targets
versions.summary: A guest that draws into targets of its own names them on its frame-end, with the view and projection it drew with; a host corrects the draws into them (RFC 0003 §4, for Cesium from a guest page).
